c: deep sea fishing south east queensland
gold coast brisbane sunshine coast fishing
half day fishing charter south east queensland
family fishing trips south east queensland
intro: South East Queensland's fishing charters run from the Gold Coast Seaway in the south, through Moreton Bay at Brisbane, to Mooloolaba, Caloundra and Noosa on the Sunshine Coast. Offshore boats fish subtropical reefs for snapper, pearl perch, teraglin, kingfish, amberjack and cobia, and in the warmer months troll for mahi mahi, mackerel, wahoo, tuna and marlin.

Every offshore trip here crosses a bar: the Gold Coast Seaway, the South Passage between Moreton and North Stradbroke islands, or the Caloundra and Noosa bars. Inside, the Broadwater, Moreton Bay, the Pumicestone Passage, the Brisbane River and the Noosa River give calm-water options for flathead, bream, whiting and mangrove jack.
season: Reef fishing runs all year, with snapper and pearl perch at their best through the cooler months (both are closed to take from 15 July to 15 August). From about September to February warmer water brings mahi mahi, mackerel, wahoo, tuna and marlin closer in. Humpback whales pass from about June to October and are often seen from fishing boats.

items: Gold Coast
Boats leave the Spit at Main Beach or Runaway Bay Marina; half days fish reefs about 10-20 km out, full days 10-35 km out in 50-95 m
Brisbane and Moreton Bay
Mostly full days from Manly or Sandstone Point, crossing the bay to the Point Lookout reefs, Cape Moreton and Flinders Reef
Sunshine Coast
Noosa, Mooloolaba and Caloundra boats fish Sunshine Reef, North Reef and Chardons Reef out to the Barwon Banks and the Hards

p: Run times differ a lot across the region. Gold Coast half-day reefs are 15-30 minutes from the Seaway, while Brisbane boats need about 1 hour 15 minutes to reach the grounds beyond the South Passage bar, which is why most Brisbane offshore trips are full days.
items: Gold Coast inshore and wider reefs
Snapper, pearl perch, teraglin, tuskfish, cobia and mackerel; black marlin can turn up about 6 km out
Point Lookout reefs and the Cathedrals
Canyons and drop-offs off North Stradbroke Island for snapper, pearl perch, kingfish and amberjack
Cape Moreton, Deep Tempest and Square Patch
Snapper and pearl perch grounds off the northern end of Moreton Island
Flinders Reef and Hutchinsons Shoals
Further reefs and shoals worked by Manly-based boats
Barwon Banks
A reef system about 23 km long, 40 km+ off Caloundra, for pearl perch, snapper, red emperor, amberjack and kingfish
Sunshine Reef, North Reef and Chardons Reef
Noosa's half-day and winter snapper grounds, about 30-45 minutes from the bar
The Hards
Wide grounds in 50-100 m reached on nine- and 12-hour trips from Noosa and Caloundra

p: If the bar is rough or you have young children, calm-water charters stay inside on sheltered estuaries and bays.
items: Gold Coast Broadwater, Nerang River and Jumpinpin
Flathead, whiting, bream, tarwhine, mangrove jack, tailor and trevally
Pumicestone Passage
Behind Bribie Island, fished from Sandstone Point and Pelican Waters, for flathead, bream, whiting and tailor
Moreton Bay and the Brisbane River
Lure fishing for snapper, flathead, jewfish and threadfin salmon on small private boats
Noosa River
Flathead, bream and mangrove jack in the river and its lakes

p: Shared offshore trips across the region usually run five, seven or nine hours, with 12-hour trips from Caloundra and Mooloolaba. Published 2026 prices start at about $200-$245 per person for a five-hour shared reef trip and $320-$360 for a full day, while whole-boat private charters start from $1,840 for a Gold Coast half day for eight anglers. Calm-water family trips start from about $109 per person.

Bars decide whether trips go, so most operators confirm the afternoon or evening before and may cancel at short notice. Rain on its own rarely stops a trip; strong wind and swell do. Catch handling varies: some crews clean and bag fish, others keep them whole, so bring an esky and leave it in the car.

Moreton Bay is a zoned marine park (Scarborough Reef is a yellow zone and Scotts Point a green zone), and Noosa operators point anglers to Great Sandy Marine Park zoning. Queensland has no general recreational fishing licence for tidal waters, but size and possession limits apply on every boat.

faq: Can you reach the reef on a half-day charter in South East Queensland?

Yes, on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast. Gold Coast half days fish reefs about 10-20 km out, 15-30 minutes from the Seaway, and Noosa half days fish Sunshine Reef and North Reef about 30-45 minutes away. From Brisbane the run beyond the South Passage bar is longer, so most offshore trips there are full days.
Where can families fish in calm water in South East Queensland?

The Gold Coast Broadwater, the Pumicestone Passage behind Bribie Island and Moreton Bay are the main calm-water options. Charters from Runaway Bay, Sandstone Point and Pelican Waters run short trips for flathead, bream and whiting, and some offer child prices.
When is snapper season in South East Queensland?

Snapper are caught all year, but the bigger fish and best bites are in the cooler months from late autumn through winter. Snapper and pearl perch are closed to take in all Queensland tidal waters from 15 July to 15 August.
Do South East Queensland charters go game fishing?

Some do, mainly in summer. Gold Coast operators target marlin, mahi mahi, wahoo and tuna from about November to February, and Brisbane charters often switch to trolling when the East Australian Current makes bottom fishing difficult.

in: on the Fraser Coast and around Bundaberg
intro: Between Rainbow Beach and Bundaberg, K'gari (Fraser Island) and the Great Sandy Strait shape the fishing. Rainbow Beach and Tin Can Bay boats run full days to the reefs off Double Island Point and southern K'gari for snapper, pearl perch, coral trout and red emperor. Hervey Bay, sheltered from the south-easterlies by the island, is known for sight fishing the flats for golden trevally and longtail tuna on fly or lure.

Further north, Bundaberg's deep-water port at Burnett Heads has no bar crossing, so boats reach reefs from a few miles out to about 50 nautical miles at the shelf. This is where southern and northern species overlap: snapper and whiting share the water with coral trout, Spanish mackerel, queenfish and threadfin.
season: Snapper move into Hervey Bay from late autumn and peak in mid-winter (snapper and pearl perch are closed 15 July-15 August). Longtail tuna are strongest from about February to May, and golden trevally, queenfish and Spanish mackerel fire in late winter and spring. Reef trips from Rainbow Beach and Bundaberg run all year, weather permitting.

p: Rainbow Beach trips leave between about 5 and 5:30am and operators confirm conditions the day before, so book flexible accommodation. Hervey Bay's channels are shallow and can be dangerous on a strong outgoing tide, while Bundaberg's port has no designated bar and no tidal restrictions.

Hervey Bay and the Great Sandy Strait sit in the Great Sandy Marine Park, so check the zoning map if you fish on your own. Bundaberg is roughly the southern limit of the coral reef fin fish spawning closures (latitude 24 50' S).

faq: Is Hervey Bay or Bundaberg better for reef fishing?

They suit different trips. Bundaberg charters run to coral reefs out toward the shelf for coral trout and red emperor, with no bar to cross. Hervey Bay charters are mostly small sportfishing boats chasing golden trevally, longtail tuna, queenfish and winter snapper in sheltered water.
Can you go fishing off K'gari (Fraser Island) on a charter?

Yes. Rainbow Beach boats fish reefs off southern K'gari, Hervey Bay guides fish the island's western side, Rooneys Point and Breaksea Spit, and some Hervey Bay charters collect guests from Kingfisher Bay Resort by arrangement.
Are there half-day fishing trips on the Fraser Coast?
In Hervey Bay and Bundaberg, yes. Rainbow Beach and Tin Can Bay charters run full days only, leaving about 5-5:30am and returning mid-afternoon.

n: Southern Great Barrier Reef & Capricorn Coast
in: on the Southern Great Barrier Reef
c: southern great barrier reef fishing charters
intro: The Great Barrier Reef begins off the Town of 1770 and Agnes Water, and from there north to Yeppoon the charters fish the southern reefs: the Capricorn and Bunker Group, the Swain Reefs and, on the longest trips, the Coral Sea. Targets are classic reef fish such as coral trout, red emperor, red throat emperor, nannygai and sweetlip, with Spanish mackerel trolled off the reef edges.

Trip styles differ by port. 1770 day boats cross the shallow Round Hill Creek bar on the tide to reach reefs within about 15 nautical miles. Gladstone is the main base for multi-day liveaboards, and Rosslyn Bay near Yeppoon offers both day trips in Keppel Bay and week-long Swains liveaboards.
season: Reef fishing runs all year outside the coral reef fin fish spawning closures (8-12 October and 6-10 November in 2026). 1770 locals rate about May to October best, with red emperor schooling on the Fitzroy Reef pinnacles, and Gladstone operators rate early spring as peak Swains season. Barramundi in the estuaries are closed 1 November-31 January.

p: Day charters from 1770 and Yeppoon supply rods, bait and tackle and suit beginners. Liveaboards from Gladstone and Rosslyn Bay are mostly self-guided: you bring your own gear, fish from dories or tenders, and the catch is processed and frozen to take home. You often need a recreational boat licence to drive a dory, and many boats need a full group or let individuals join set trips.

Almost all the offshore grounds are inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, and the Capricorn and Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones, including most of Heron Island and part of Wistari Reef. Charter skippers fish the open zones; on your own boat, check the current GBRMPA zoning map.

Agnes Water is about 5.5 hours' drive from Brisbane, Gladstone about six hours or an hour's flight, and Yeppoon about 45 km from Rockhampton. If the Round Hill Creek bar or the weather rules out a 1770 trip, Bundaberg and Gladstone boats also fish the southern reefs.

faq: Where is the closest Great Barrier Reef fishing to Brisbane?

The Town of 1770 and Agnes Water, about 5.5 hours' drive north of Brisbane, sit where the Great Barrier Reef begins. Day charters there fish reefs within about 15 nautical miles, and the Capricorn and Bunker Group lies roughly 45-75 km offshore.
How do you fish the Swain Reefs?

On a liveaboard. Boats leave Gladstone or Rosslyn Bay near Yeppoon, steam overnight about 120 nautical miles to the Swains, and fish for about a week, usually from dories. Some Yeppoon day boats reach the Swains on 18-36-hour extended trips in settled weather.
Can I fish around Heron Island?

Mostly no. Heron Island is largely green zone and part of neighbouring Wistari Reef is green zone, so fishing isn't allowed there. Open zones exist elsewhere in the Capricorn and Bunker Group, and charter skippers know where you can fish.
